title: Streaming Relay for Toolchains with Staged Result Injection and Recursion Hysteresis
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:

We currently support tool/function calling and streaming at the API layer, but multi-tool chains that mix streaming responses and blocking tool invocations expose subtle hazards: unexpected recursion when a tool triggers a new orchestration run, partial output leaks when a downstream tool fails mid-stream, and difficulty reconciling structured outputs with incremental token emissions. This ticket defines a streaming-aware relay for toolchains that performs staged result injection (safe, schema-checked insertion of tool outputs) and a hysteresis-based recursion guard to avoid oscillating re-invocations across tool boundaries.

Goals:
- Allow handler chains to stream tokens to clients while orchestrating blocking tool calls without stalling the stream for unrelated tokens.
- Ensure tool outputs are injected into the agent context atomically and validated against declared structured output schemas.
- Prevent recursive loops across tool-invocation boundaries with a hysteresis mechanism that records recent invocation ancestry and enforces cooldowns rather than hard halts (improves graceful degradation for legitimate repeated flows).
- Provide observability hooks to trace partial-stream boundaries, injection events, and recursion gate firings for debugging and postmortem.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change backend kernel execution or batching policies; it interfaces with the existing serving runtime.
- Not addressing cross-customer isolation for Dedicated/Private in this change; follow-up will map the gating to tenant quotas.
proposal:
Architecture overview:

1) Streaming Relay Layer: introduce a lightweight relay that sits between the model output generator and the network streaming sink. The relay buffers semantic boundaries (sentence/JSON schema) and allows token passthrough for non-tool frames while temporarily pausing stream boundary emission when a blocking tool call is initiated that will mutate the context.

2) Staged Result Injection: when a tool returns, the relay validates the tool payload against the declared structured-output schema (JSON Schema subset). Validated results are staged into a transactional injection buffer. Once the injection point (a named anchor in the prompt/context) is confirmed, the relay commits the buffer and emits a compact injection marker into the stream so downstream consumers (clients or connectors) can reconcile the insertion. If validation fails, the relay emits an error frame with remediation hints instead of raw tool text.

3) Recursion Hysteresis Guard: maintain an invocation ancestry sliding window (recent N tool ids + timestamps) per session. Instead of immediate termination upon detecting an ancestor in the chain, compute a cooldown score that grows exponentially with repeated re-entry within a short window. When cooldown exceeds threshold, gate the invocation and emit a user-visible guard frame recommending a fallback model or human review. The hysteresis approach reduces false positives for legitimate retries while preventing runaway recursion.

4) Compatibility Layer: provide a compatibility shim so older SDKs/clients that expect plain token streams still receive token frames. Newer clients can opt into structured frames (e.g., {"injection": {"anchor":"step-3","id":"tool-x","payloadRef":"tool-xyz"}}) via a negotiated streaming-protocol header.

Trade-offs considered:
- Buffering introduces small latency spikes at tool boundaries; mitigated by only buffering semantic boundaries and allowing non-related token passthrough.
- Full JSON Schema validation is expensive; we will implement a constrained subset with fast path checks (required fields + type checks) and a slow path for deep validation used in debug mode.
- Hysteresis parameters are heuristics; we will tune in production and make them tenant-configurable behind feature flags.

References:
- Design notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFER/pages/StreamingRelayDesign (internal doc)
acceptance_criteria:
- Relay correctly streams non-tool token frames with <10ms median additional latency at 95th percentile except during tool commit events.
- Staged injections must pass schema fast-path for 95% of production tool responses; slow-path validation must not block the main event loop (processed in an off-ramp worker).
- Recursion hysteresis prevents >99% of infinite-loop incidents observed in synthetic fuzz tests while allowing legitimate re-invocations in 80% of real-world retry traces.
- Backwards-compatible: legacy clients receive token-only streams; opt-in clients receive structured injection frames.
- Instrumentation: traces exist for boundary events, injection commits, validation failures, and gate firings with sampling at 100% for first hour after deploy then 1% steady-state.
- End-to-end automated tests and a canary run on a subset of runtime-1.22 pods for 48 hours with traffic shadowing enabled.
implementation_notes:
Implementation plan (phased):

Phase 1 (dev): implement relay prototype as a middleware in the executor process that can be toggled via runtime flag. Include a minimal JSON schema fast-path validator (required/type only). Add unit tests for streaming passthrough and injection commit semantics.

Phase 2 (staging): wire staged injection buffer to the context store, implement injection marker frames, add hysteresis tracker persisted in memcache per session. Add integration tests with the tool runner to validate payload flows.

Phase 3 (canary): enable on 5% of runtime-1.22 pods, enable full observability dashboards. Run fuzz tests that simulate recursive tool-chains, long-running streams, and structured output errors.

Phase 4 (rollout): increase traffic to 25%/50%/100% with monitoring thresholds to auto-rollback if recursion gate firings spike or latency regressions exceed thresholds.

Testing notes:
- Add deterministic unit tests for injection commit/rollback when validation fails.
- Add property-based tests to generate tool-chains and detect cycles.
- Create a synthetic workload that reproduces past infinite-loop incidents from incident logs (link below).

Observability and instrumentation:
- Emit events: STREAM_BOUNDARY_PAUSE, TOOL_CALL_INIT, TOOL_CALL_RETURN, INJECTION_COMMIT, INJECTION_FAIL, RECURSION_GUARD_FIRED.
- Add dashboard: streaming-relay-latency, injection-validation-fail-rate, recursion-guard-rate, staged-buffer-depth.

Migration & compatibility:
- Header negotiation: clients set Accept-Streaming-Frames: structured or token-only. Default remains token-only.
- SDK patches (JS/Python/Go) to support structured frame parsing will be released in tandem (PRs linked in comments).
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Schema mismatch may block urgent tool outputs. Mitigation: error frames include sanitized raw payload and a remediation hint; operators can toggle to permissive validation under emergency.

Risk: Hysteresis parameters too aggressive block legitimate loops. Mitigation: expose parameters per-tenant and provide an override API for on-call. Also increment backoff to safe default before hard-blocking.

Risk: Increased memory usage for staged buffers. Mitigation: enforce per-session buffer caps and LRU eviction policy with clear metrics and alerts.

Risk: SDK fragmentation (clients not upgraded). Mitigation: maintain token-only compatibility and document structured frame contract clearly in release notes.
